title: Notify Me When Done
bottom_line: Type /ntfy:notify-me with a condition. Claude carries on with the work and sends a push notification once that condition has genuinely been met.

sections.heading: Type the command with the moment you want a push

blocks.caption: The command and its argument. The condition is the moment you want to hear about.

blocks.title: What happens after you press Enter

nodes.label: You name a condition
nodes.note: For example "when you finish the implementation" or "if the tests fail".

nodes.label: Work continues
nodes.note: Claude continues with the work already in progress or requested in this conversation.

nodes.label: Push sent
nodes.note: Sent at priority 4 (high) unless you named another priority.

blocks.text: Claude does not fake completion. It sends the notification only once the condition has genuinely been met.

sections.heading: Have a subscribed app and your settings ready

cards.title: An ntfy app
cards.text: An ntfy app or web client subscribed to your topic, to receive the notifications.

cards.title: Saved plugin settings
cards.text: Your `server` and `topic`, saved once with `/plugin configure ntfy@wovemind` (or the dialog shown when the plugin is enabled).

blocks.caption: Run /ntfy:configure, or ask "set up ntfy on my phone", for a step-by-step walkthrough of all three.

blocks.title: The two plugin settings
rows: The ntfy server every notification is published to. Point it at your own instance if you self-host.
The topic notifications go to unless you name another one in a request.

blocks.text: The defaults only take effect after you save the dialog once. Until then the command (and the ntfy skill) falls back to `https://ntfy.sh` and `claude` itself, except when the token file `~/.ntfy` exists (see stop 4).
On public ntfy.sh anyone who knows the topic name receives its messages, so pick a long random topic name there.

sections.heading: You can also set the priority and topic in that line

blocks.title: What Claude reads from what you type
rows: When to send the notification, for example "when you finish the implementation" or "if the tests fail".
min, low, default, high or urgent, or 1 to 5.
A topic you name here wins over the `topic` setting.
The `topic` setting, or `claude` if it was never saved.

before.label: Default
before.text: /ntfy:notify-me when you finish the implementation sends at priority 4 (high).

after.label: Your choice
after.text: Name a priority in the command, for example `urgent`, and that priority is used instead.

sections.heading: The push goes to your saved server, with one safety stop

blocks.title: How the server is chosen
blocks.caption: The token in ~/.ntfy may belong to another server, so Claude stops instead of sending.

blocks.text: When it stops, Claude tells you to run `/plugin configure ntfy@wovemind` and set `server`: to your own server, or to `https://ntfy.sh` if that is where your token belongs.

When the command runs unattended, called from another skill such as plan-tools `drain-issues` or compliance-audit `apply`, it skips the notification and says so in the report instead of stopping that skill.

sections.heading: A good push says what happened in one line

cards.title: Title
cards.text: A short context label, for example the task or repo name.

cards.title: Message
cards.text: One line that states what happened, for example "Implementation finished — all tests passing".

cards.title: Priority
cards.text: 4 unless your condition or arguments say otherwise.

blocks.caption: What the notification on your phone contains.

blocks.text: Claude sends it with the plugin's `ntfy-send` script, or with the ntfy skill's curl pattern if the script is not available.

next_action.text: Type /ntfy:notify-me followed by the moment you want to hear about, such as "when you finish the implementation".
next_action.detail: For a step-by-step setup of the app and the plugin settings, run /ntfy:configure or ask "set up ntfy on my phone".
